April 4, 21.

Sir,

With reference to your telegram of February 24,
copies of which together with replies are attached,
I have the honour to inform you that a Russian
bearing the name of Morris Reuter was arrested by
the Municipal Police on March 25 and has been
sentenced to six months imprisonment. He had in
his possession certain photographic films (copies
enclosed) which point to a connection with the
counterfeit Bank notes said to be manufactured and
circulated by Poznikoff, Markin and Utevsky.
Reuter has stated that he was furnished with the
films in question by Utevsky who is now in Harbin
and I should be obliged if you would be good enough
to communicate with the Police of that place and
enquire if they have any knowledge of this man who
left Shanghai without a passport and apparently
travelled to Harbin by rail notwithstanding the fact
that the Authorities all along the line were notified
immediately of his departure. We now hold a warrant
for his apprehension and if it would be effected in
any way perhaps some way could be found of having
him brought to Shanghai for trial.
As the necessity of communicating direct with
the Police of Harbin in connection with the numerous
bad characters who travel continually between that
place and Shanghai is steadily growing greater, I
have to ask you to be kind enough to ascertain if
there is no possibility of making arrangements which
would enable me to deal directly with the Chinese
Authorities, who, I believe, are now in charge of
the Police administration there.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Commissioner of Police.

The Military Governor
of Sungkiang and Shanghai.

1921年4月4日。

先生，

关于您2月24日的电报，其副本及回复附后，
谨此奉告，一名名为莫里斯·罗伊特 (Morris Reuter) 的俄国人
于3月25日被工部局警务处逮捕，并已被
判处六个月监禁。在他身上发现了一些摄影底片（副本附后），
这些底片表明他与据称由波兹尼科夫 (Poznikoff)、马尔金 (Markin) 和乌捷夫斯基 (Utevsky)
制造和流通的伪造钞票案有关联。
罗伊特声称，上述底片是由目前身在哈尔滨的乌捷夫斯基提供的，
如蒙阁下惠允与当地警方联系，
查询他们是否了解此人的情况，本人将不胜感激。此人未持护照离开上海，
尽管沿线当局已立即获知其离境消息，但他显然仍乘火车前往哈尔滨。
我们现在持有对他的逮捕令，如果能够通过某种方式将其抓获，
或许可以找到办法将他引渡至上海受审。
由于就那些频繁往返于该地与上海之间的众多不良分子一事，
直接与哈尔滨警方沟通的必要性日益增加，
本人不得不恳请阁下查明，是否有可能作出安排，
使我能够直接与中方当局打交道，据信，目前那里的警务行政工作
已由中方当局负责。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

警务总监。

松江上海镇守使。

March 26th 1921.

REPORT ON Arrest of Russian in Possession of Material for
making False Bank-notes.

Made by D. I. Cruickshank Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

I beg most respectfully to report, that, at 11 p.m.
25th March 1921 I arrested Morris Reuter, Russian Compositor
Russian Echo Office Seward
in the Road. The arrest was as follows:

Some times ago a Russian named S. Sudakoff residing at
No 3 Astor Terrace gave information to the Police, that, he
had received photographs of Yen Bank-notes from Morris Reuter
for the purpose of making false money. This photographs I
have in my possession, Sudakoff has requested me several times
to return them to him. As Reuter might suspect him of giving
information, this I declined to do, but put him off on
different excuses, but simply waiting for developments.

About 7 p.m. tonight Reuter met Sudakoff on Range Road
and demanded his photographs, but on being refused, he
violently assaulted Sudakoff knocking him to the ground,
whereby he was rendered unconscious. Sudakoff came to the
Hongkew Station and reported the assault to me. Consequently
in company with D. S. Conduit I immediately searched for and
arrested Reuter and afterwards searched his room at No. 36
Chapoo Road, where I found a book, which between the outside
covers contained several photographs of Bank-notes secretly
concealed therein.

At first Reuter denied all knowledge of these photographs
but afterwards frankly admitted the whole business, and said
he got the photographs from a Russian named S. Utevsky in the
Great Eastern Hotel about 6 weeks ago for the purpose of
making false money.

（左侧手写批注：）
Russian Hotel
He living in
the same.

关于逮捕一名持有制造假钞材料的俄国人的报告。

由侦探督察克鲁克香克 (D. I. Cruickshank) 撰写，经刑事情报处处长转发。

先生，

卑职谨此恭敬地报告，1921年3月
25日晚上11点，我逮捕了莫里斯·罗伊特，他是《俄罗斯回声报》(Russian Echo) 的俄籍排字工，
住址在西华德路 (Seward Road)。逮捕经过如下：

前一段时间，一名居住在阿斯特台 (Astor Terrace) 3号的俄国人 S. 苏达科夫 (S. Sudakoff) 向警方提供情报，称他
收到了莫里斯·罗伊特提供的日元钞票照片，
目的是用于制造假币。这些照片目前在我手中，苏达科夫曾多次请求
我将照片归还给他。由于罗伊特可能会怀疑是他提供了情报，
我拒绝了这一请求，只是以各种借口推脱，
静待事态发展。

今晚约7点，罗伊特在兰路 (Range Road) 遇见苏达科夫，
索要他的照片，但在遭到拒绝后，他猛烈殴打苏达科夫，
将其击倒在地，导致其昏迷。苏达科夫来到
虹口巡捕房，向我报告了这起殴打事件。因此，
我与侦探警佐康杜伊特 (D. S. Conduit) 一起立即搜寻并
逮捕了罗伊特，随后搜查了他在乍浦路 (Chapoo Road) 36号的房间，
在那里我发现了一本书，其封面夹层中秘密藏有几张
钞票的照片。

起初，罗伊特否认知道这些照片的存在，
但后来坦白了整个事情，并说
大约6周前，他在礼查饭店 (Great Eastern Hotel) 从一名叫 S. 乌捷夫斯基 (S. Utevsky) 的俄国人那里得到了这些照片，
目的是用于制造假币。

December 2, 1920

My dear little chicken,

My repeated requests for a letter from you have been declined on the excuse that you are lazy. I regret I cannot accept this explanation and have to state frankly that I am offended. It was indeed a surprise when Mr. Alexander Nikolayevich visited me. We met in the house of the Labutin family, and we never spoke of the past. You can imagine my astonishment and - I shall not hide it - my pleasure when the aim of his official visit was revealed to me. It is quite incomprehensible how it happened that you recalled me to your mind, but I am more interested in the consequence than the cause.

We have heard that you have no "work", and I wish you success in your "unemployment". I have also been informed that you travel extensively and appear like a meteor in different points of two Empires, but you only avoid our country. What fault have we committed to deserve such treatment ? You may be sure that many hearts are beating forcibly for you my dear little chicken. The beatings of these friendly hearts are,□□□ in their gladness at the hope of seeing you, like the workings of a fa□ier's bellows. Let us pray that you will not fo□get to visit Shanghai where you will meet with a warm welcome. The Labutin family has left Shanghai. This made the town empty and mournful. But I remained here, and it would take too long to explain my reasons for do'ng so. It is difficult to say if I could have done better. A little "yes" enables me to suffer

1920年12月2日

我亲爱的小鸡，

你以懒惰为借口，拒绝了我多次去信的请求。很遗憾，我不能接受这个解释，必须坦率地说，我感到被冒犯了。当亚历山大·尼古拉耶维奇先生 (Alexander Nikolayevich) 来访时，我确实感到惊讶。我们在拉布京 (Labutin) 一家家中相遇，我们从未谈论过去。你可以想象我的惊讶，以及——我不隐瞒——当得知他正式访问的目的时，我的喜悦。实在难以理解，你是怎么想起我的，但我更关心结果而非原因。

我们听说你没有“工作”，祝你在“失业”中取得成功。我还获悉你四处旅行，像流星一样出现在两个帝国的不同地点，但你唯独避开我们的国家。我们犯了什么错，竟要遭受如此对待？你可以确信，许多心都在为你剧烈跳动，我亲爱的小鸡。这些友好心灵的跳动，□□□ 充满了见到你的希望带来的喜悦，就像铁匠的风箱在运作。让我们祈祷你不要忘记访问上海，在那里你会受到热烈的欢迎。拉布京一家已经离开上海。这使得城市变得空旷而凄凉。但我留了下来，解释我这样做的原因需要太长时间。很难说我是否能做得更好。一个小小的“是”让我能够忍受

patiently a large "no". I remain here with the intention
of working, and am now employed as lady corrector in the
Russian Echo. I am free all day, but labour at night.
I have moved to a room close to the printing office and
feel the better for it. I think you will not make me
wait long for your answer. If you do I shall be awfully
angry and never write again.

Your little woman,
E. Zaovsky,
20 Nanzing Road.

To-day I received a report from the Shanghai
Municipal Police to the effect that three Russians
named Utevsky, Markin and Poznikoff, who have
been staying at the Great Eastern Hotel and who
are suspected of being concerned in the manufacture
of counterfeit Japanese yen notes left by rail for
Tientsin at 9 a.m. to-day. The last named is
accompanied by his wife. An associate named
Klenboard left for Tientsin yesterday. The first
mentioned three men have no huchow and may carry
counterfeit yen notes or films for printing on
their persons or □□□□ in their luggage. Utevsky
is 29 years of age, short stature and clean shaven.
Markin is 35 years of age, tall and small moustache.
Poznikoff is 44 years of age, strong build and
brown beard. Klenboard is 39 years of age, stout
build and clean shaven. The S.M. Police have
asked me to wire you requesting you to search for
and detain these men. I accordingly wire you
and request you to order your men to trace and
arrest the Russians and reply.
February 24.

Sir,

A watch was kept on the Russians named Utevsky, Markin, Klenboard and Poznikoff from Feb. 20 until Feb. 24 when they left for Tientsin. On Feb. 20 all four attended the evening performance at the Victoria Theatre. On Feb. 21, Markin visited Tong Sung( 夏升 ) Stationary Shop, No. 3294 Seward Road, where he remained for ten minutes. On the same evening he visited a boarding-house at No. 20 and 21 Miller Road kept by a Chinese. At 10.15 a.m. Feb. 22 Markin and Poznikoff visited the International Banking Corporation, No. 1A Kiukiang Road. At 10.30 a.m. the same day Utevsky and Klenboard visited No. 7 N. Honan Road, the home of Dorfman, a well known opium smuggler. At 3.45 p.m. that day Markin and Poznikoff made some purchases in the Wing On Store, and later went to 85 Range Road (Haskell Road?). At 4.20 p.m. Feb. 22 Poznikoff visited 53 Range Road and about the same time Markin called at No. 20 and 21 Miller Road. In the evening of that day, Markin visited No. 26 Chapoo Road. At 9.30 a.m. Feb. 23 Klenboard left for Tientsin. At 10.30 a.m. on that day Markin and Poznikoff visited No. 53 Range Road where they had tiffin. About 7.30 p.m. Feb. 23 Poznikoff took four large boxes to No. 1650 Haining Road, a house occupied by Chinese.

REPORT ON Presence of Gang of Bank Note Forgers in Shanghai.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by

Sir,

It has now been ascertained that the member of the gang of counterfeiters of Japanese notes who lives at No. 26 Chapoo Road is one Riter, who works in the Russian Printing Co. on Seward Road. A man named Poznikoff, who lives with his wife in the Great Eastern Hotel, is also believed to be connected with them.

Besides the above gang, which is interested in 100 Yen notes, it is stated that there are some people in Shanghai who belonging to another group which makes 10 Yen notes. A Chinese who is connected with a boarding-house at No. 43 Range Road and Miss Greenberg, who keeps a tailor shop near the Hongkew Bridge, are said to be members of the latter group.

On the morning of February 19, one Lieutenant D. N. Anapkin, who had an introduction from Mr. N. B. Ramsay, called at the Japanese Consulate and stated that if given a sum of money, he could buy counterfeit Japanese bank notes. Anapkin is Agent of the U. S. February 21 1921

REPORT ON Presence of Gang of Bank Note Forgers in Shanghai.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

According to a Russian, who wishes to remain anonymous for the present, a band of Japanese bank note forgers consisting of four Russian Jews and a German is at present in Shanghai. This band has all the paraphernalia necessary for making spurious 100 yen notes of the Bank of Chosen, and it is thought that they will soon start operations if they have not done so already. Three of the gang named Utevsky, Markin and B.Kenboard live in the Great Eastern Hotel, and a fourth whose name has not yet been ascertained resides at No. 26 Chapoo Road. The informer claims to have partially gained the confidence of the latter who has given him for safe keeping half a dozen photo films of the notes in different stages of manufacture. He showed these in proof of the genuineness of his story, but declined to give them to the police on the ground that the forger at any moment might ask to have them handed back. The informer believes that a careful watch kept for a few days on the members of the gang will disclose evidence of their plans. This watch has been started, and further inquiries are being made.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I. Givens
D. I.

D. C. I.

REPORT ON Alleged Forgery of Japanese Bank Notes.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by

Sir,

In view of a suggestion that the information about the alleged manufacture locally of spurious yen notes of the Bank of Chosen, which seems to be supported by the failure of the Police to make any headway with their investigation of the matter, a report of an interview with the Chief of the Finance Section of the bank in question which appeared in the Osaka Asahi Shimbun on Nov. 14, is of interest :-

"It is nothing but a rumour that counterfeit notes of the Bank of Chosen are in circulation.

It has been reported that some Russian Bolsheviks and recalcitrant Koreans made counterfeit notes of the Bank of Chosen, a great quantity of which was brought to Japan. The Chief of the Finance Section of the Bank has made the following statement to our correspondent on this subject :-

"When the rumour started this Spring, we requested the authorities and banks to send us any false notes they found, but we have not received any up to date. If the rumour were true, we should be the first to know about it. We, however, have received no such news. It is true that two 50-sen defaced notes were found by the Tsuruga Bank, but this was a very trifling matter. My opinion is that some Bolsheviks or Koreans using the rumour of last Spring and the discovery of the two 50-sen notes found by the Tsuruga Bank as a basis have set this new report in circulation".

The Police Department of the Governor-General of Chosen considers the rumour a joke."

concerned in the making of false money, Messrs
Shivriansky and Livchitz are well known locally.
The former has visited Shanghai several times during
the past three or four years. He usually stops at
the Kalee or Savoy Hotels, and people who come into
contact with him have formed the opinion that he is
engaged in some sort of dishonest business. He is
intimate with David Gabrueler, a former runner of
the Kalee Hotel, who is now reported to be in Harbin,
and a Miss Zikin who is at present in Shanghai.
Efforts are now being made to locate her address.
Confidential information received by the Police in
November 1919 indicated that some one connected with
Miss Jewell's school might be concerned in making
spurious notes, and in this connection it is noteworthy
that two brothers named Sherevansky belonging to a
Harbin Jewish family are boarders in that establishment.

曾向日本领事馆提供情报的杜姆巴泽（Doombadze）是一名格鲁吉亚人。他约9个月前来到此地，与两名同胞合伙在百老汇路1044号开设了一家寄宿公寓。他现已与该机构断绝关系，过去一个月一直居住在乍浦路26号。据所知，他为人相当诚实，但目前经济状况不佳。在涉嫌参与制造假币的人员中，希夫里安斯基先生（Mr. Shivriansky）和利夫奇茨先生（Mr. Livchitz）在当地颇有名气。前者在过去三四年间曾多次访问上海。他通常入住卡利酒店（Kalee Hotel）或萨伏伊酒店（Savoy Hotels），与其接触的人认为他从事某种不诚实的生意。他与大卫·加布鲁勒（David Gabrueler）关系密切，后者曾是卡利酒店的跑街（runner），据报现在哈尔滨；他还与目前在上海的齐金小姐（Miss Zikin）关系亲密。目前正努力查找她的住址。警方在1919年11月收到的机密情报显示，朱厄尔小姐学校（Miss Jewell's school）的相关人员可能参与制造假钞，值得注意的是，属于哈尔滨犹太家庭的谢列万斯基（Sherevansky）两兄弟是该机构的寄宿生。

( 5 )

I.R. Livchitz, a reputed smuggler and a harbourer
of smugglers, has resided in Shanghai for several years,
and now lives at No. 26 Seward Road. Although he has
a large family and consequently would not be likely
to engage in crimes which, if discovered, would be
likely to entail a long term of imprisonment, it is
possible that he or some of his associates are connected
with the spurious note traffic.

Pinigin, who is reported to be a friend of Livchitz,
Provsik alias Pluszik and Petresco were reported to
be in Siberia last September. It has been alleged that
they brought a large number of spurious bank notes to
Shanghai about July or August.

The Police have been enquiring for a considerable
time regarding the manufacture of spurious bank notes,
but their efforts have been fruitless.

Further enquiries are proceeding and any information
obtained will be communicated to you in due course.

I have the honour to be,

据报为利夫奇茨朋友的皮尼金（Pinigin），以及普罗夫西克（Provsik，又名普卢兹克 Pluszik）和佩特雷斯库（Petresco），据报去年9月在西伯利亚。据称他们于7月或8月左右将大量假银行券带至上海。

警方已就制造假银行券一事进行了相当长时间的调查，但 efforts 均无果而终。

Sir,
No substantiation has so far been obtained of the infor-
mation that spurious yen notes are manufactured in Shanghai,
and no attempt seems to have been made to alter these notes
here. The Shanghai Municipal Police experience great diffi-

Sir,

I beg most respectfully to report re the attached
correspondence.

This is the same old tale, formerly it was Roubles,
but now it is Japanese money, I have had this alleged infor-
mation for several months, but on exploring the root of the
information, I always find either jealousy about women, opium
smuggling, or some other cause. Other information simply to
obtain money on a good story, but such information is never
certain, just enough to leave you in doubt. Last week I
received information, that, a man named F. Schichman, a Russian,
had come to Shanghai to remove a large quantity of forged

named Emanuel B. Sousitchman attempted to murder Schichman on
the 26th April 1920 by shooting at him with a revolver whilst
entering a cinematograph show on North Szechuen Road. The
trouble was over some women affairs and the idea of conveying
this information to me was to get Schichman arrested to avenge
Sousitchman's grievance.

find substantial proof. He is undoubtedly a smuggler. All

taken with great caution. I have practically had the same
information as given in the attached correspondence, but I

Made by D. S. I. Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,
    Despite careful and persistent inquiries, no confirmation can be found of the information that spurious rouble notes are being printed in Shanghai. The persons whose names are given in the secret report forwarded by the Consul General for Russia are, with a few exceptions, well known pimps and opium smugglers The money they make in this way not only affords them means to live in comparative ease, but enables them to put aside something for their old age, and when detected smuggling no serious consequences follow. On the other hand they may be able to make more money by counterfeiting rouble notes, but the chances of being found out are greater, and the consequences when detected would be infinitely more serious. Considering all the circumstances, it seems to me extremely unlikely that such an astute lot of individuals would agree to embark on such a problematical venture as counterfeiting, when a life of ease and comparative luxury is assured to them by smuggling, which may be indulged in without fear of serious consequences. It also seems to me that if such a large number of unprincipled men knew that counterfeiting of rouble notes was taking place, some one of their number would have long since denounced his confederates.

REPORT ON Printing of Spurious Rouble Notes.

Made by D. S. I. Givens.    Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,
    Enquiries have failed so far to elicit any confirmation of the allegation that spurious rouble notes are being printed in Shanghai, neither has anything come to light which would assist in establishing the identity of the three Poles, the Japanese and the Chinaman alleged to be concerned in making them.
    A record of the movements of Stone of the Wen Pun (回本 ) Soap Factory, 968 Tatung Road, who has been watched since 5th instant, is attached, and there appears to be nothing suspicious in his behaviour. The Rbls 30,000:00 given by Mendelsen through the Yokohama Specie Bank to Stone were, according to the latter, in payment for 246 boxes of soap supplied. Mendelsen and his friend Markin had also been negotiating with Stone with a view to becoming his partners in the soap factory. This concern is now partially financed by the Oriental Press, and it was the intention of Mendelsen and Markin to buy over that company's interest in the business.
    Ettinger, one of those suspected in connection with the counterfeiting of rouble notes, is said to be living at the Yamato Hotel, Changchun, at present. His wife left here on 9th instant with the intention of joining him. M. Goldman, another suspect, left here on 10th instant, and his wife went away from Shanghai nine days previous to that date. Mr Sharmins, a 3rd suspect, who is looking after Goldman's house, states that the latter went to Mukden, and that his wife went to Japan.

Secret report .

Three poles are said to be engaged in manufacturing forged 1000
rouble-notes of the Omsk Government , besides one japanese and a chinaman.
The buyers are residents of Harbin known as :# Volodka Grek" "Sigis-
mund Rumyn" "Mancilo" and "Goldstein" . The notes are concealed in trunks
between clothing .
Others belonging to the gang are Mishka Poliakoff , recently married
in Shanghai .
Two men called Meschan and Fasel Gush , residents of Changchun are sa
said to have already taken over the quantity of forged notes ordered by
them.
Others who have ordered notes are Gersch Stambler , a foreigner ,
Ettinger the Turc , Leiba Kater , Moisha Goldman , Shaminsky , a Brazili-
an citizen and Vidgop a Russian Jew ( besides Mr. Markin and the late Mr.
Mendelson , staying at the Palace Hotel.
The 1000 rouble-notes ordered amount to at least 2.000.000 roubles .
Meschan , Senka Kosoi , Beilin or Singer are supposed to have left
Shanghai on July 27th for Harbin . The Consulate General has wired to the
Russian Consul at Changchun about it .
"Volodka Grek" was the first to take some of these notes to Harbin.
He and his accomplices Mancilo , Sigismund Rumyn and Goldstein are suspec
ted to have entered into connection with railway and bank cashiers .
Fishman and Schwarzman ( the latter's nickname being Provodnik )
are awaiting the completion of the order for banknotes in Shanghai .
Meschan is a nickname. This man was recently married and the wedding
took place at Mr. Goldman's house. He must be known to the Consulate ha -
ving had to take out a marriage licence . He presides at Changchun and
is an opium smuggler . The notes , as the opium are concealed in a double
bottom .
Ettinger is one of the principal members of the gang. He , Gersh
Stambler ( a nickname ) Leib Kater ( also a nickname ) Moisha Goldman ,
Haim Grinberg ( nickname Homal ) are waiting for the 2.000.000 roubles
ordred to be ready. Vitgob is said to have order notes for 1.000.000

秘密报告。

据称有三名波兰人、一名日本人和一名中国人从事制造鄂木斯克政府的一千卢布伪钞。买家是哈尔滨的居民，名为：“Volodka Grek”、“Sigismund Rumyn”、“Mancilo”和“Goldstein”。钞票藏在衣箱的衣物之间。
该团伙的其他成员包括 Mishka Poliakoff，最近在上海结婚。
据称，居住在长春的两名男子 Meschan 和 Fasel Gush 已经接管了他们订购的那批伪钞。
其他订购钞票的人包括外国人 Gersch Stambler、土耳其人 Ettinger、Leiba Kater、Moisha Goldman、巴西公民 Shaminsky 以及俄罗斯犹太人 Vidgop（此外还有住在宫殿酒店的 Markin 先生和已故的 Mendelson 先生）。
订购的一千卢布钞票总额至少为 2,000,000 卢布。
据推测，Meschan、Senka Kosoi、Beilin 或 Singer 已于 7 月 27 日离开上海前往哈尔滨。总领事馆已就此向驻长春的俄罗斯领事发电。
“Volodka Grek”是第一个将部分此类钞票带到哈尔滨的人。他和他的同伙 Mancilo、Sigismund Rumyn 和 Goldstein 被怀疑与铁路和银行出纳员建立了联系。
Fishman 和 Schwarzman（后者的绰号为 Provodnik）正在等待上海完成钞票订单。
Meschan 是一个绰号。此人最近结婚，婚礼在 Goldman 先生家中举行。他必须为领事馆所知，因为他不得不申请结婚许可证。他在长春主持事务，是一名鸦片走私者。钞票像鸦片一样藏在夹层底板中。
Ettinger 是该团伙的主要成员之一。他、Gersh Stambler（绰号）、Leib Kater（也是绰号）、Moisha Goldman、Haim Grinberg（绰号 Homal）正在等待订购的 2,000,000 卢布准备就绪。据说 Vitgob 订购了价值 1,000,000

roubles .

If Ettinger , Grinberg and Stone are watched it should be easy to
discover the factory of the notes.

Stone lives 45 Boone Rd . He talked about this business to a man Leo-
noff ( nickname Nunchik Ochakover ) but the latter refused to have any-
thing to do with it saying that he prefers smuggle opium .

Mishka Poliakoff is waiting for Meschan at Changchun and will take
the notes to Harbin . Smugglers from Harbin , who used to carry opium
have all gone over to the smuggling of forged banknotes.

Headquarters are 1) at the Goldman's. Other places where the gang
meets are 2) at Gersh Stambler's . Grimberg is staying there, and some
time Leib Kater 3) at Vigob's ( nickname Yold ) .

A Mrs Reuter ( Seward Rd 32 ) has taken a small quantity to Har -
bin. She also smuggles opium . If at Kwangchentze station these people
will be searched the smuggling will be made impossible. Only it is nece-
ssary to examine the bottom and the sides of the trunks .

The two million order will be taken over for sale by Ettinger.
"Volodka Grek" owns a house in Harbin and is considered as the protec-
tor of all the thieves .

One of the principal meetings places is now Sharmin's
shop on Broadway . Sharmins is now a Brazilian citizen . He used to
be a Russian. Mashka Chemodan and Rose Fetterman (alias Margarite Shar-
mins , Shaminskaia)Ettinger , Gersh Stambler , Goldman , Kater have
placed a big order which will be ready in two weeks. Great secrecy is
kept about the people who are executing the order . Only Stone and Et-
tinger visit the factory , the others are afraid of going there. Old
Fuchsman seems also to be of the gang . He was in jail in Japan for
forging money.

If Ettinger and Stone were handed over to the Chinese Police they
might find out where the factory is . Stone is said to be a British
subject . The notes are made at the latter's soap Factory .

The samples are now ready and the whole order will be executed
by Mr. Stone next week .

卢布的钞票。

如果监视 Ettinger、Grinberg 和 Stone，应该很容易发现钞票工厂。

Stone 住在布恩路 45 号。他曾向一个叫 Leonoff（绰号 Nunchik Ochakover）的人谈论过这项生意，但后者拒绝参与，说他更喜欢走私鸦片。

Mishka Poliakoff 正在长春等待 Meschan，并将把钞票带到哈尔滨。来自哈尔滨、过去从事鸦片运输的走私者都已转而走私伪造钞票。

总部设在 1) Goldman 家。团伙聚会的其他地点有 2) Gersh Stambler 家。Grimberg 住在那里，Leib Kater 有时也住在那里；3) Vigob 家（绰号 Yold）。

一位 Reuter 夫人（西华德路 32 号）曾携带少量钞票前往哈尔滨。她也走私鸦片。如果在广宁子站搜查这些人，走私将无法进行。只需检查衣箱的底部和侧面即可。

这两百万的订单将由 Ettinger 接管销售。
“Volodka Grek”在哈尔滨拥有一处房产，被视为所有窃贼的保护者。

目前主要的聚会地点之一是百老汇路的 Sharmin 商店。Sharmins 现在是巴西公民。他以前是俄罗斯人。Mashka Chemodan 和 Rose Fetterman（别名 Margarite Sharmins, Shaminskaia）、Ettinger、Gersh Stambler、Goldman、Kater 下了一大笔订单，将在两周内准备好。对于执行订单的人员保密工作做得非常严密。只有 Stone 和 Ettinger 去工厂，其他人不敢去那里。老 Fuchsman 似乎也是该团伙的成员。他曾在日本因伪造货币而入狱。

如果将 Ettinger 和 Stone 移交给中国警察，他们可能会找出工厂在哪里。据说 Stone 是英国臣民。钞票是在他的肥皂厂制造的。

样品现已准备好，整个订单将于下周由 Stone 先生执行。

Harbin, July 29th 1919.

To the Inspector Mr Cruikshanks.

I have the pleasure to inform you, Mr Cruikshanks, that
a Roumanian named Zigmund Forshmit, at present a French
subject, who is well known to you was in Shanghai 4 weeks
ago and brought with him one million false Siberian 500
Rouble notes to Harbin.

The money is printed in Shanghai in partnership with a
certain Russian subject Mrs Goldstein, who resides in Harbin.

I beg to inform you, that Z. Forshmit is leaving soon
for Shanghai to take delivery of false money and draw your
attention to look after him.

I may also inform you that many Russian merchants from
Harbin are at present in Shanghai, some of them in first
class hotels and all of them are waiting for false money,
as the printing press is very busy at work. Several
million false Siberian Roubles have been brought lately
to Harbin from Shanghai.

I am, etc.
Russian citizen
G. Shwartzberg.

哈尔滨，1919 年 7 月 29 日。

致 Cruikshanks 督察先生。

Cruikshanks 先生，我很高兴地通知您，一个名叫 Zigmund Forshmit 的罗马尼亚人，目前是法国籍，为您所熟知，他于 4 周前在上海，并带了一百万张伪造的西伯利亚 500 卢布钞票到哈尔滨。

这些钱是与一位居住在哈尔滨的俄罗斯籍女士 Goldstein 合伙在上海印刷的。

谨此通知您，Z. Forshmit 即将前往上海接收伪钞，提请您注意对他进行监视。

我还可以告知您，许多来自哈尔滨的俄罗斯商人目前在上海，其中一些人住在头等旅馆，他们都在等待伪钞，因为印刷机正忙于工作。最近有几百万张伪造的西伯利亚卢布从上海运到哈尔滨。

此致，等。
俄罗斯公民
G. Shwartzberg.

July 18th 19

CONFIDENTIAL.

Sir,

With reference to your letters Nos. 89, 109,
112 and 115 on the subject of forged rouble
Omsk Government notes which, it is alleged, are
imported from Shanghai into the territory of the
Chinese Eastern Railway via Changchun, I have the
honour to inform you that Michael Doll is still
in prison and that it will be another year before
the sentence expires.
We have not been able to ascertain whether
he had any relations with Mr. Koff alias Mikhailovsky
and enquiries made regarding the other persons
mentioned in your letters have not elicited
any proof that they are connected in any way
with the printing of forged rouble notes.
I should be glad if you could obtain a
specimen of the forgeries in question as it might
assist us in the continuance of further enquiries
and in locating the establishment where the
notes are printed.
Reverting to the arrest of the two Russians
Jimbirsky and Zilberstein, who were charged with
breaking into the premises of the Mikimoto pearl
store on December 10th 1918 and remitted to the
Court at Vladivostock, I would be much obliged
if you would inform me of the result of the trial.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
（签名）
for Captain Superintendent of Police.

V. Grosse, Esq.,
Consul General for Russia.

Sir,
I respectfully beg to report with reference to
attached File No.5272/5 referring to suspects in connection
with printing and circulating counterfeit Rouble Bank Notes
and paragraph referring to Occupant of No. 26 East Seward
Road, a Russian Jew named E.K.Livchitz.
Livchitz denies keeping a Boardinghouse and that no one,
other than his family and relatives has resided there for
the past 5 months.
As regards the Printing Machinery, in February 1918
a Russian Jew named M.Wrighter arrived from Russia and
resided at No.26 East Seward Road. He obtained employment
as a Printer at the Russian Publishing and Printing Coy,
No.5 Thorne Road. Through him Livchitz sold the Machinery
and Russian Type to that Company, which was removed by
Wrighter on handcarts during July 1918.
Livchitz is a Commission Agent and a dealer in
secondhand goods, frequents Auction Rooms and exhibits a
signboard in Russian at his residence.
In conjunction with his Commission Business he meets
the arrival of so called Russian Merchants, arranging for
the disposal of merchandise they have to sell or place them
in touch with dealers in merchandise they may require.
These so called Russian Merchants are and have been
suspected of being dealers in smuggled opium.
He is a prominent member of the Synagogue, but not
a Rabbi.

由副督察普罗瑟（D.S.I. Prosser）撰写。转呈

先生，
谨就附件第5272/5号卷宗呈报，该卷宗涉及印刷和流通伪造卢布钞票的嫌疑人，以及其中提及的西华德路（Seward Road）东段26号住户、一名名为E.K.利夫奇茨（E.K. Livchitz）的俄罗斯犹太人的相关段落。
利夫奇茨否认经营寄宿公寓，并称在过去5个月内，除其家人和亲属外，无人居住于此。
关于印刷机械，1918年2月，一名名为M.赖特（M. Wrighter）的俄罗斯犹太人从俄罗斯抵达，并居住在西华德路东段26号。他在索恩路（Thorne Road）5号的俄罗斯出版印刷公司受雇为印刷工。通过他，利夫奇茨将机械和俄文铅字出售给该公司，这些物品于1918年7月由赖特用手推车运走。
利夫奇茨是一名佣金代理人和二手货商，常出入拍卖行，并在其住所悬挂俄文招牌。
结合其佣金代理业务，他会迎接所谓的俄罗斯商人到来，安排处理他们待售的商品，或让他们与可能需要这些商品的经销商建立联系。

REPORT ON Men suspected in connection with printing and
circulating false rouble notes.

Made by D.I. Reeves. Forwarded by Chief Detective Office.

Sir,

I beg to report that careful enquiries have been made
about the manufacture of false rouble notes, and so far nothing
very definite can be found out, as regards the place of printing
or the person responsible for the printing. It is clear however
that if these notes are printed in Shanghai it is done very
secretly and as there has not been any reports of any false
rouble notes being put into circulation here, although there is
a great business done locally in buying and selling rouble notes them, it
shows that they are taken north and disposed of, most possibly
in the purchase of opium in Chan Chung and Harbin. The
difficulty in this case is the publicity which would immediately
arise if persons who know some of the names mentioned, were
questioned as regards the manufacture of the notes, and the
chance of locating the printing press would be spoilt; and as
this is the main objective to proceed with the enquiries at
all, it must be done very secretly.

As regards the first letter No. 80, from the Russian
Consul General, M. Doll received two years imprisonment and is
still in custody and will be for the next 12 months. Mr. Koff
alais Mikhailoosky has been located. He is at present living
at 14 Quinsan Gardens in a boarding house kept by Mrs. Weinstock,
who is registered in the Russian Consulate. He lived for a time
with Mr. Makaroff at 3 Young Allin Terrace who is a Russian
Lawyer. This man Koff has been previously charged in Harbin
in connection with the forgery of notes. Makaroff describes

先生，

谨报，已对伪造卢布钞票的制造情况进行了仔细查询，但截至目前，关于印刷地点或负责印刷的人员，尚未发现非常确切的线索。然而，很明显，如果这些钞票是在上海印刷的，那么过程是非常秘密的；尽管本地买卖卢布钞票的业务量很大，但这里没有任何关于伪造卢布钞票进入流通的报告，这表明它们被运往北方处置，最有可能是在长春（Chan Chung）和哈尔滨用于购买鸦片。本案的困难在于，如果询问知晓上述部分姓名的人员关于钞票制造的情况，会立即引起公众关注，从而破坏定位印刷机的机会；而既然这是开展调查的主要目标，就必须非常秘密地进行。

关于第一封信件第80号，来自俄罗斯总领事馆，多尔（M. Doll）先生被判两年监禁，目前仍在羁押中，并将继续服刑12个月。科夫（Koff）先生，又名米哈伊洛夫斯基（Mikhailoosky），已被找到。他目前居住在昆山路花园（Quinsan Gardens）14号的一家寄宿公寓内，该公寓由温斯托克夫人（Mrs. Weinstock）经营，她在俄罗斯领事馆有登记。他曾与马卡罗夫（Makaroff）先生在杨氏别墅（Young Allin Terrace）3号同住过一段时间，马卡罗夫是一名俄罗斯律师。这个叫科夫的人此前在哈尔滨曾因伪造钞票被指控。马卡罗夫形容他是一个骗子和鸦片走私者。尚不清楚

With regard to the second letter No. 109; Mendelson is once again residing in the Palace Hotel and seems to have plenty of money. He is not registered at the Russian Consulate, but registers himself at the Hotel as a Russian. Mr. Goldstien also lived at the Palace Hotel but left for Dalny on the Sakaki Maru on the 1st inst.

Mrs. Goldstien the wife of Mr. Goldstien was living two months ago at 26 Seward Road in a Russian boarding house kept by a Russian Jew named "Lipshitz". Lipstitz at one time kept a small printing establishment on the Woosung Road. He still has the machinery at his house. He is a Rabbi and used to kill the chickens etc. for the Jews. He now appears to have plenty of money and can afford to send his family to Japan whereas at one time he was remarkably poor. Mrs. Goldstien left for Dalny where she no doubt was joined by her husband. J. Korenblit and E. Gutzan we have no information about.

As regards the third letter No. 112, the Mr. Stone referred to as a dealer in soap is no doubt the Mr. A Stone who was printer at the jail. He does a kind of auction broker business and possibly has sold soap which he had bought at Auctions. He now has a boarding house No. 45 Boone Road. He is a British Subject and is closely connected with Russians as he speaks the language and being a printer by trade, and having a good knowledge of the northern ports he is the man who is the most likely to be closely associated with the printing of the notes. The man Markin is unknown to us.

戈尔茨坦先生的妻子戈尔茨坦夫人两个月前还住在西华德路26号的一家俄罗斯寄宿公寓，该公寓由一名名为“利普希茨”（Lipshitz）的俄罗斯犹太人经营。利普希茨曾在吴淞路经营一家小型印刷所。他的机器仍然放在家里。他是一名拉比，过去常为犹太人宰杀鸡等家禽。他现在似乎很有钱，有能力送家人去日本，而以前他非常贫穷。戈尔茨坦夫人前往大连，毫无疑问她在那里与丈夫汇合。关于J.科伦布里特（J. Korenblit）和E.古赞（E. Gutzan），我们要没有相关信息。

关于第三封信件第112号，信中提到的作为肥皂商人的斯通（Stone）先生，无疑就是曾在监狱担任印刷工的A.斯通（A Stone）先生。他从事某种拍卖经纪业务，可能出售了他在拍卖会上购买的肥皂。他现在在博恩路（Boone Road）45号经营一家寄宿公寓。他是英国臣民，与俄罗斯人关系密切，因为他会说俄语，且职业是印刷工，对北方港口有深入了解，他是最可能与钞票印刷有密切关联的人。我们对马尔金（Markin）此人一无所知。

As regards 4th letter No. 115, none of the persons mentioned are known to us, or to have resided in Shanghai. Wilhelm Gotzel may have been in Shanghai, as a Russian whose name is unknown came here some two years ago and started a studio in painting and photography. He lived for a time with Kremle. He may be the man referred to.
As I have not seen or heard of any false rouble notes being circulated in Shanghai it would help us considerably if some specimens of the false ones could be shown us and points of difference in the forgeries and the genuine ones pointed out. I would suggest that search warrants be issued to search the premises of Lipshitz, 26 Seward Road, Koff, alias, Nekhailovsky at 14 Quinsan Gardens, Mendelson at the Palace Hotel, and A Stone at 45 Boone Road. If false notes were found it would then give us something to work upon.
